title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!












View this post on Instagram



A post shared by Uncle Paul (@unclepaul.music)

title: Sunday Sounds | Sean Gaskell
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for an afternoon of music and art in the Museum. With a soundscape of the West African kora harp, we invite you to experience artwork in the galleries in a more emotional and sensory way. 
ABOUT THE MUSICIAN
Sean Gaskell features songs on the kora- a 21 stringed West African harp. He studied under the extensive instruction of Moriba Kuyateh and the late Malamini Jobarteh in Gambia, and both Youssoupha Cissokho and Mamadou Cissokho in Senegal. The kora is traditionally played by oral historians known as Griots. Many songs featured on the kora preserve an 800-year history dating back to the founding of the Mande empire. Gaskell has presented adult, youth and family programs at over 500 libraries and a multitude of k-12 schools, colleges, universities and assisted living facilities throughout the United States and Canada. 
For more information, please visit www.seangaskell.com

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, January 5  |  9 – 10:30 am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Starting in the classroom, you will get a chance to learn best practices for using binoculars, try out spotting scopes, and look at different field guides. Later in class, we’ll move outside and practice observing birds around the buildings and core garden area. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair, we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Botanical Drawing for Beginners
description:
Botanical Drawing for Beginners
with Camille Daunno 
Four Sessions: 
Tuesdays, January 5, 12, 19, and 26 | 9:30 am – 12:30 pm 
Register Here!
Discover the fundamentals of botanical drawing in this welcoming beginner-level class. During this four-week series students will learn essential drawing techniques including contour drawing, line work, shading and texture. Through guided instruction and observation, students will build confidence in capturing the shapes, patterns, and details found in nature while developing their own artistic style. All materials are provided, and participants will leave with in-progress and completed works as well as new skills to continue their botanical drawing practice at home. 
Camille Daunno is a retired Art Teacher with an undergraduate degree in Fine Art with graduate work in Textile Design. She worked in NYC as a designer for 10 years designing Fabric and wallpaper. Camille studied Art in NJ, NYC and Italy and studied Botanical Illustration and Painting at the NY Botanical Gardens with a certified instructor. Her favorite audience to share her love of Botanical art with is her children and grandchildren.

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

### The Lowdown:

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.
* **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Envisioning the New Year with Creativity & Vision Board-Making
description:
Envisioning the New Year with Creativity & Vision Board-Making
with Catherine Willows 
Thursday, January 7  |  12 – 4 pm 
Register Here!
A new year opens like a blank canvas, inviting us to awaken our imagination and explore what we wish to create, experience, and welcome into our lives. The first New Moon following Winter Solstice offers a beautiful moment for renewal, fresh perspective, and envisioning new possibilities. As the returning light begins to illuminate the winter landscape, we, too, can begin to see what is ready to emerge. Gathering at the Arboretum, we’ll connect with the rhythms of Nature and the Creative Life Force through guided reflection and intuitive art-making. Beyond traditional goal-setting or vision boarding, this is an invitation to open a creative portal into the possibilities of a new cycle. Through collage, painting, color, imagery, symbols, and words, you’ll create a personal vision board expressing the inspiration and possibilities drawing you forward. No art experience is needed—just curiosity, an open heart, and a willingness to explore. 
Art supplies will be provided. Please bring magazines or images to cut and paste, along with a journal. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. 
Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Listening through the Seasons: Introduction to Soundscapes
description:
Listening through the Seasons: Introduction to Soundscapes
with Meg Worthington 
Friday, January 8 | 1 – 3:30 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
How does the Arboretum sound in winter? What can we learn by listening closely? 
Join us as we launch a yearlong exploration of the NC Arboretum’s changing soundscape. In this introductory session, participants will discover the field of soundscape ecology, learn how scientists use sound to study ecosystems, and practice techniques for deep listening and observation. Together, we’ll visit our first listening station, collect baseline observations, and begin documenting the sounds of winter. 
Listening Through the Seasons is a yearlong community science and soundscape ecology project at the NC Arboretum. Participants will help document the changing sounds of the Arboretum throughout the year while learning about ecology, biodiversity, and the art of deep listening. Through field observations, sound recording, and guided activities, we’ll create a seasonal acoustic portrait of the Arboretum and contribute to an ongoing research project exploring how natural soundscapes change over time. 
This program includes instruction both inside a classroom and outside following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for at least half of the class. 
 Meg Worthington (they/them) is an educator, artist, and lifelong learner whose work is rooted in curiosity, creativity, and connection to the natural world. They began teaching in Alaska while earning a Master’s degree in Outdoor and Environmental Education, where they discovered a passion for creating meaningful experiences that inspire wonder and exploration. Working on a small educational farm in Palmer, Alaska, deepened Meg’s appreciation for the relationships between people, place, and community. Today, they are enjoying the opportunity to learn more about the unique ecology of Western North Carolina and are excited to teach as an Adult Education Specialist at The NC Arboretum. As a local Asheville artist, Meg creates zines, collages, and mixed-media works that explore human emotion, personal growth, and our search for meaning. Nature is a constant source of inspiration in their creative practice, and they delight in experimenting with new materials, techniques, and art forms.

title: Hello My Dear
description:
Hello My Dear is the acoustic duo of Caitlin Krisko and Aaron Austin (of Caitlin Krisko & the Broadcast), delivering soulful, roots-driven originals and covers steeped in blues, Americana, and classic rock. Hello My Dear offers a warm, high-impact performance that feel both powerful and deeply personal. Rooted in the songs and spirit that have defined their journey together the duo presents a more stripped-down, emotionally resonant expression of the music of Caitlin Krisko & The Broadcast, alongside carefully curated covers that have shaped their sound. At the heart of Hello My Dear is Caitlin Krisko's unmistakeable voice, equal parts raw power and ender storytelling, paired with Aaron Austin's soulful, dynamic guitar work. Described by Rolling Stones as "one of the best-kept vocal secrets of the southeast," Krisko brings the same vocal gravity and emotional honesty that has earned widespread acclaim in the band's full electric setting, translated beautifully into an acoustic format. Come join them for Hello My Dear's performance at Asheville's own, Jack of the Wood. Music 8:30-11:30pm, $10 cover at the door.

title: Introduction to Stargazing
description:
Introduction to Stargazing
with Steve Martin 
Saturday, January 9  |  3 – 6 pm Classroom, 7:30 – 8:30 pm Stargazing 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Discover the wonders of the night sky in this beginner-friendly course combining classroom learning and outdoor stargazing. Learn to find stars, constellations, and planets using simple tools, and get tips for observing with binoculars and telescopes. No experience or equipment needed! 
This program will take place both inside the classroom and outside, following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for part of the program time. 
Steve Martin is an astronomer and educator who has taught astronomy, physics and sustainability at colleges, universities, and learning centers across the country for over 35 years. He has worked as an instrument specialist for the Hubble Space Telescope and as Observatory Supervisor at Williams College, where he participated in international research expeditions studying solar eclipses. An engaging speaker and educator, Steve offers stargazing experiences, astronomy courses, and workshops exploring the wonders of the universe, dark sky science, and the connections between astronomy, ecology, and sustainability.

tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Intermediate Birding at NC Arboretum
description:
Intermediate Birding at the NC Arboretum
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, January 12  |  9 – 10:30 am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Bring your binoculars and favorite field guide, during this intermediate class we will wander farther away from the buildings and core gardens to really immerse ourselves in the wide world of birding! Discussions will center around more intermediate topics such as seasonal characteristics and patterns of common birds and migration patterns. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum. 
●  Pre-registration is required for all classes unless otherwise detailed above. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions. 
●  See a full listing of Adult Education Programs at the North Carolina Arboretum here! Questions? Check our FAQs. 
●  We are committed to fostering a diverse, supportive learning community. If the cost of a class is a barrier for you, please complete this scholarship form and we will see what kind of assistance we can provide. 
●  Follow us on Facebook & Instagram! Or join our Adult Education Student Hub on Discord!

title: Snow Country by Yasunari Kawabata
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
**At an isolated mountain hot spring, with snow blanketing every surface, Shimamura, a wealthy dilettante meets Komako, a lowly geisha. She gives herself to him fully and without remorse, despite knowing that their passion cannot last and that the affair can have only one outcome. In chronicling the course of this doomed romance, Kawabata has created a story for the ages—a stunning novel dense in implication and exalting in its sadness.**

title: Streams & Creeks of the Arboretum
description:
Streams & Creeks of the Arboretum
with Lauren Lampley 
Thursday, January 14  |  1 – 4 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Join Lauren on an exploration of the NC Arboretum’s streams and creeks to learn about how they play an important role in our park’s ecology. We will take the opportunity to look at maps of how the rivers of our region shaped the mountains and valleys before going out into the field to follow a stream until it reaches the French Broad River. 
This program will take place in the classroom and outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department. 
●  Pre-registration is required for all classes unless otherwise detailed above. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions. 
●  See a full listing of Adult Education Programs at the North Carolina Arboretum here! Questions? Check our FAQs.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:

Led by Founding teacher Ronya Banks or AIM Facilitator Wallace Bohanan, our Thursday evening group meditation sessions will continue to consist of a guided meditation (30 minutes), a few-minute break, a dharma talk by the teacher (30 minutes), and then Q & A/Discussion (30 minutes).

Meditation instructions will be given for beginners.

The session begins promptly at 7:00 pm. If online, please mute your audio during the guided meditation and talk.

Location

MindSpring Building
966 Tunnel Road, Asheville, NC 28805

We need your generosity now more than ever before. Please hit the Donate Button to your right and donate whatever you can afford. Or become one of our monthly sustaining donars. (The suggested minimum donation is $10, but no one is turned away for lack of funds.)

Group Meditation Guidelines

* Arrive several minutes early. You are welcome to greet others before we start.
* Turn off your cell phones and other beeping devices.
* Sit in a comfortable position, chairs are provided, bring your own cushions, blankets, or props.
* If on zoom, please mute yourself during guided meditation, and talk, and then unmute yourself to share during the discussion.

title: Fishes of the Southern Appalachians
description:
Fishes of the Southern Appalachians
with Carlton Burke 
Friday, January 15  |  12 – 4 pm 
BRN – Wildlife Core 
Register Here!
The Southern Appalachian region is rich with a variety of fish species. These include not only the better known species of game fish that we love to catch for sport or food, but also include an incredible diversity of smaller, lesser-known non-game fish, which play an important role in the ecology of our aquatic mountain habitats. In this class we will discuss many of the fish species found in the mountain region and learn about their classification, habitat, life cycles, and their identifying features. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: Winter Buds & Bark Tree ID
description:
Winter Buds and Bark
with Lauren Lampley 
Saturday, January 15  |  1 – 4 pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
Ever wondered how you can identify a tree without its leaves? All tree species have different patterns of bark and leaf/flower buds that can be used to identify them even in winter time. In this program, we will look closely at the common trees around the NC Arboretum trails and point out specific characteristics of their buds and bark so you can identify them even without their leaves. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

description:
Tickets are officially on sale for the 2027 Mars Hill University Baseball Night fundraiser. Hosted by the 2026–2027 Lions baseball team, this special evening brings our program’s biggest celebration of the year to downtown Asheville. 
Get tickets 
Event Details: 
Date: Saturday, January 16, 2027
Time: 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM
Location: HomeTrust Park (Downtown Asheville, NC) 
Featuring Keynote Speaker Jim Holland 
We are thrilled to welcome Jim Holland—author, civic leader, and 2019 Appalachian League Hall of Fame inductee—as the keynote speaker for our 2027 event. 
Jim brings insights from an extraordinary 30-season career (1990–2019) in southern West Virginia baseball. He is best known for his 24-year tenure (1992–2015) as General Manager of the Princeton, WV Appalachian League franchise, an affiliate of both the Cincinnati Reds (5 seasons) and Tampa Bay Rays (19 seasons). During his time in Princeton, 85 future Major League players passed through his clubhouse. 
Jim’s front-office tenure also included stops with the Huntington Cubs (1990–1991) and the summer collegiate West Virginia Miners of the Prospect League (2016–2019), as well as serving as Corporate Secretary and an executive committee member for the Appalachian League. 
Career Accolades & Hall of Fame Honors: 

Double Hall of Famer: Inducted into both the Appalachian League Hall of Fame—alongside legends like Cal Ripken Jr., Greg Maddux, Eddie Murray, Dale Murphy, C.C. Sabathia, Nolan Ryan, and Andruw Jones—and the West Virginia Sports Legends/Artie Museum in 2019.
League Recognition: Named Appalachian League Executive of the Year (1993), recipient of the Appalachian League President’s Award for long-term service (2015), and the only five-time winner of the league’s Award for Promotional Excellence.
Community Leadership: Honored with the Rotary Club of Princeton’s Service Above Self Award and named the 2012 Citizen of the Year by the Princeton-Mercer County Chamber of Commerce.

Following his retirement from baseball in May 2020, Jim published his acclaimed memoir, My Fortunate Detour (2022), chronicling his journey through the game. A 1976 two-sport letterman at Dunbar High School and a 1980 cum laude graduate of the University of Charleston (B.A. in Mass Communications), Jim resides in Princeton, WV, with his wife, Judy. Their son, Warren Hypes, carries on the family’s baseball legacy as Vice President of Creative and Brand for the Tampa Bay Rays. 
Join us at HomeTrust Park for an unforgettable night of baseball stories, community, and support for our student-athletes.

title: The JackTown Ramblers
description:
The JackTown Ramblers, hailing proudly from Morganton, NC, embody the true spirit of bluegrass music with their infectious energy and deep-rooted passion. Consisting of four musicians with a deep history in the music, they have carved out a name for themselves as stalwarts of the local music scene, captivating audiences with their distinctive blend of swingy bluegrass and traditional mountain melodies. Formed with a shared love for their craft, The JackTown Ramblers are known for their dynamic performances, delivering somewhere between 75 and 100 shows annually. Each member brings a unique flair to their music, creating a synergy that resonates with listeners far and wide. Their repertoire spans both time-honored classics and original compositions, showcasing their versatility and dedication to the genre. Whenever on stage, The JackTown Ramblers exude a genuine enthusiasm for their music, infusing every note with heartfelt sincerity and joy. Their live performances are characterized by lively instrumentation, tight harmonies, and a palpable sense of camaraderie that invites audiences to join in the celebration and fun. In Morganton and beyond, The JackTown Ramblers have become synonymous with high-energy, soul-stirring bluegrass and swinging mountain music. With each show, they continue to leave an indelible mark on their listeners, embodying the essence of what it means to play music from the heart.

title: The Leadership Lounge
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
You want to do your best work every time. It's important to you, and you care about how you show up and what your team thinks of you.
Being present for ourselves is a significant challenge that often creates a gap. This gap represents the difference between the way we aspire to live and how we actually live. We choose to bridge this gap because it is the right thing to do.

Introducing a great way for new nomads to connect and discover important key takeaways for their lives. As a new Asheville Digital Nomad, where do you go if you don’t know many people?

You will participate in a discussion, yes! YOU, the audience, will be a part of a wonderful panel discussion. Whether you are a veteran or a newbie, come to **The Leadership Lounge**. You will get something out of this event and gain new insights to improve your outlook on how well you are settling into Asheville and Western North Carolina.

**The Leadership Lounge** presents a fabulous evening: **The Three Pillars.** This special occasion will introduce you to new actions to manage burnout and physiological changes, combining practicality with an intuitive desire for more fun.
**Pillar I - Somatic Sovereignty**: Lindsay Coward
**Pillar II - Self-Leadership**: Stacy Antos
**Pillar III - The Sovereign Career**: Jane Carter

***Special discount* on 'ADN'-engraved Pirani cups! 5th-anniversary custom ADN Pirani cups!**
**Available in 16 oz, 26 oz, and 32 oz for $15, $20, and $25.**

Everyone! Whether you're leading in for-profit, non-profit, academia, community organizations, or entrepreneurship – or simply curious about leadership – you're welcome to join us.

* Free Parking
* Beverages: Alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages

Come join us. Meet new people. Take away some next steps.

description:

with Lauren Lampley 
Wednesday, January 20  |  1 – 3 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Ever wondered why our storm systems almost always come from the west? Or why certain faces of mountain slopes are dryer than others? Sometimes while we study the ecology of a landscape, we forget that this small region we are studying is just a part of a global system. During this class we will look at how global wind patterns and ocean currents affect the amount of rainfall that we get here in Western North Carolina from year to year. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Landscape Design Fundamentals
description:
Landscape Design Fundamentals
with Jennifer Verprauskus 
Two sessions: 
Friday, January 22  |  1 – 3:30 pm and 
Friday, January 29  |  1 – 3:30 pm 
BREG – Core 
Register Here!
Students will learn the fundamentals of landscape design in a two-part class that introduces participants to design principles, site assessment and planning, among other topics. Gain a better understanding of what comes into play in creating and managing sustainable and aesthetically appealing landscapes. We will also brush on some basic permaculture design practices. You will come away empowered to be more creative, instinctive, decisive and purposeful in understanding good design and more adept at recognizing what’s not. 
Jennifer Verprauskus is a North Carolina Licensed Landscape Architect and a Permaculture Design Certificate Holder. She studied Landscape Architecture at the University of Massachusetts & Cal Poly. Since graduating, she has traveled the world to help people grow trees and their own food. She is the founder of both UpBeet Landscapes and BareRoot Designs, PLLC. 
●  Pre-registration is required for all classes unless otherwise detailed above. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions. 
●  See a full listing of Adult Education Programs at the North Carolina Arboretum here! Questions? Check our FAQs. 
●  We are committed to fostering a diverse, supportive learning community. If the cost of a class is a barrier for you, please complete this scholarship form and we will see what kind of assistance we can provide. 
●  Follow us on Facebook & Instagram! Or join our Adult Education Student Hub on Discord! 
●  Interested in supporting the NC Arboretum more directly? Donate to the ONE Fund here.

title: The B-Sides
description:
The B-Sides are a five-piece rock-soul fusion band that was born out of late-night jam sessions attheir college rehearsal space within the mountains of Western NC. Blending the raw energy of rockwith the depth and groove of soul, the band has built a sound that’s both electric and heartfelt. Eachof the five members brings their own unique background and influence, creating a dynamic andsometimes quit eclectic mix of style and taste.



Now stepping beyond the campus stages of Montreat and into the professional music world, the



B-Sides are dedicated to carving out their own space. Their music is about connection; aboutbringing people together in the same way they were brought together in the first place.Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Remedy Tree
description:
Remedy Tree is a Florida-based Americana band rooted in bluegrass, old-time, and folk traditions. Founded in 2015 by Gabriel and Abigail Acevedo, the group blends Gabriel’s unique perspective—born in Puerto Rico and raised in rural Florida—with Abigail’s deep old-time background. Together with Nathan Beaumont on mandolin and Isaac Taylor on banjo they create original music that feels both timeless and fresh. Since signing with Mountain Fever Records in 2024, Remedy Tree has performed at Ireland, England, and all over the Eastern US sharing stages with notable acts such as Peter Rowan, The Infamous Stringdusters, Sister Sadie, Ricky Skaggs, and The Steeldrivers. Their 2025 album Beyond What I Can See continues to gain momentum as they headline The Forest Tour in the Summer of 2026. A growing force in Americana music—deep roots, new ground.

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

### The Lowdown:

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.
* **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

Led by multi-instrumentalists and songwriters Clint Roberts and Jackson Grimm, Asheville’s Holler Choir blends a distinctly Appalachian indie-pop sound with haunting harmonies, stirring string arrangements, and heart-wrenching ballads—yet rarely conforms to a single genre. Rooted in Old-time, Americana, and Bluegrass traditions, Holler Choir’s sound is ultimately singular by design. Alongside Roberts and Grimm, a rotating cast of gifted Appalachian musicians contributes to the group’s recordings and electrifying live performances.



Holler Choir began during the recording of Roberts’s 2022 solo EP, Mountain Air, at Asheville’s Crossroads Studios. That fortuitous gathering of roots musicians proved to be the genesis of an unmistakable new sound. Produced by Grammy Award–winning multi-instrumentalist Michael Ashworth of The Steep Canyon Rangers, the five-song EP lit the fuse, setting Holler Choir on a path to delight audiences throughout the Southeast and beyond. Much of that same collective reunited to record the band’s 2024 debut full-length album, Songs Before They Write Themselves, tracked in the historic church room at Echo Mountain Studios and engineered by Jason Richmond (Avett Brothers, Rising Appalachia).



Grimm officially joined the fold in the summer of 2024 after being invited to collaborate on Holler Choir’s Susto Stringband project, which reinterprets the indie-rock Americana songwriting of Susto’s Justin Osborne through old-time and bluegrass lenses. As Roberts and Grimm continued working together, Grimm’s sharp lyrical wit and wide-ranging multi-instrumentalism quickly proved to be a powerful addition to the band’s creative core. Holler Choir is slated to release its first collaborative record under this lineup in late 2026 or early 2027.Music 9pm-12am $10 cover at the door.

title: Johnny Mullenax
description:
Keep the Billy Strings vibes going with Johnny Mullenax in person after the show!



Johnny Mullenax, a 28-year old Tulsa native, has quickly jumped into the Americana scene in the past year, creating huge buzz with blistering live performances that are already the stuff of legend, as part of an extensive headline tour. 



Saving Country Music says, "Every single venue and festival on planet Earth should be moving heaven and Earth to get these dudes on their stage. … Johnny Mullenax can't come more highly recommended." 



Blending rock, country, bluegrass, blues, soul into blistering  jams, Mullenax takes the Tulsa sound to soaring new heights. Following the well-received 2024 EP Friend Like You, he greeted December 2025 with the brand-new single, “Couple Extra Hours,” which showed off the virtuosity and joy he brings to his craft. His latest EP, This Joint’s For You Too, continues that momentum, with singalongs that get louder as the night gets later. Come join him for a proper party during Billy Strings week!



Music 10pm-1am $15 cover at the door or buy your ticket ahead of time:https://www.eventbrite.com/e/johnny-mullenax-at-jack-of-the-wood-tickets-2005061318378

title: Re-Entry Simulation
location: Upper Fellowhip Hall
description:
A re-entry simulation places participants in the role of a “returning citizen” and asks them to complete weekly tasks—such as reporting to probation, securing housing, finding employment, accessing transportation, obtaining IDs, managing fines, and meeting basic needs. Stations represent real-world agencies and services, and participants quickly experience how limited time, financial constraints, bureaucratic hurdles, and strict supervision requirements create overwhelming barriers.

The simulation demonstrates how easily people can fall out of compliance, not because of unwillingness, but because the system is complex, inflexible, and often impossible to navigate without support. It builds empathy, deepens understanding of structural barriers, and highlights the importance of re-entry support, community resources, and fair supervision practices.

title: Doctor Zhivago by Pasternak (Pevear and Volokhonsky translation)
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
**First published in Italy in 1957 amid international controversy, Doctor Zhivago is the story of the life and loves of a poet/physician during the turmoil of the Russian Revolution. Taking his family from Moscow to what he hopes will be shelter in the Ural Mountains, Zhivago finds himself instead embroiled in the battle between the Whites and the Reds. Set against this backdrop of cruelty and strife is Zhivago's love for the tender and beautiful Lara, the very embodiment of the pain and chaos of those cataclysmic times. Pevear and Volokhonsky masterfully restore the spirit of Pasternak's original world classic.**

Troublesome Rising: Writing When the Water Recedes
description:
In Troublesome Rising: Writing When the Water Recedes, authors Melissa Helton, Robert Gipe, and Mandi Fugate Sheffel reflect on their experiences during the historic 2022 flood in Hindman, Kentucky, and their contributions to Troublesome Rising: A Thousand-Year Flood in Eastern Kentucky. Through individual presentations and a panel discussion, they will explore how creative writing can represent unthinkable loss, document the experiences of Appalachian communities, and leave room for a hopeful tomorrow. 
This event will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of Highsmith Student Union and is free and open to the public; however, registration is encouraged. Register Here 
“Troublesome Rising: Writing When the Water Recedes” is the fourth event in the “Rising Waters: Writing Place and Environment” Thomas Howerton Professorship lecture series presented by the UNC Asheville English Department. This three-year series features humanities scholars in conversation with natural sciences scholars about issues affecting us all. 
Melissa Helton 
Melissa Jørgenrud Helton is Literary Arts Director of Hindman Settlement School, a cultural nonprofit in Knott County, Kentucky. Her work has been published in Shenandoah, Women Speak, Still: The Journal, Anthology of Appalachian Writers, Norwegian Writers Climate Campaign, and more. Her chapbooks include Inertia: A Study and Hewn, and her first full length collection is A Middle-Aged Woman Rages. 
She is editor of the anthology Troublesome Rising: A Thousand-Year Flood in Eastern Kentucky which documents the deadly flood of 2022, and the literary and arts magazine Untelling. She is series editor for the Hindman Seedbed series under the Swallow imprint of Ohio University Press. Her work has been supported through the Kentucky Foundation for Women, and has been awarded the George Scarbrough Poetry Prize, the Emma Bell Miles Nonfiction Prize, has been nominated for Best of the Net, and has been a finalist for multiple awards including the Weatherford Award. 
Originally from Toledo, Ohio, she has called southeast Kentucky home since 2010. She was an educator for various colleges and universities for 17 years, and is a member of the Kentucky Poetry Society and Appalachian Studies Association. She has been honored with the Mildred Haun Award of Excellence and designation as a Kentucky Colonel for her work after the 2022 flood, and she is a dual citizen in the United Kingdom. 
Mandi Fugate Sheffel 
Mandi Fugate Sheffel was born and raised in Red Fox, KY. She graduated from Eastern Kentucky University and currently serves as the Sycamore Fund Project Coordinator at the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky. She is vice chair of the Mountain Association board. Additionally, she owns and operates Read Spotted Newt, an independent bookstore in the coalfields of eastern Kentucky. Her personal essays and opinion pieces can be found in Still: The Journal, Lexington-Herald Leader, Salon, and the Courier Journal. Her personal essay collection, The Nature of Pain, is available now through The University Press of Kentucky. 
Robert Gipe 
Robert Gipe won the 2015 Weatherford Award for outstanding Appalachian novel for his first novel Trampoline. His second novel, Weedeater,  was published in 2018. His third novel, Pop, ​was published in 2021. All three novels are published by Ohio University Press. In 2021, the trilogy won the Judy Gaines Young Book Award. From 1997 to 2018, Gipe directed the Southeast Kentucky Community & Technical College Appalachian Program in Harlan. Gipe is founding producer of the Higher Ground community performance series, and has served as a script consultant for the Hulu series Dopesick and a producer on the feature film The Evening Hour. Gipe resides in Harlan County, Kentucky. He grew up in Kingsport, Tennessee.​ 
Accessibility
UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or would like to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in the film screenings, please contact Stephanie Bullick, Director of Accessibility, at accessibility@unca.edu. 
Visitor Parking

All visitors must adhere to the University’s parking policy. Please visit the UNC Asheville Visitor Parking Permit Registration site to acquire a visitor permit to park on campus.

title: Greenwood Rye
description:
Greenwood Rye is a modern jam-grass band, formed in Nashville as the house band for the award-winning bluegrass supper club, Jane's Hideaway. Led by Shawn Spencer (Seven Handle Circus) on Guitar and Vocals, the band 's main cast features Ruth Shumway (Fiddle, Vocals), David Freeman (Mandolin, Vocals), Taylor Shuck (Banjo) & Andy Brown (Upright Bass).



The group writes fun, modern songs that are rooted in bluegrass, throwing in some jam-band tendencies, and an occasional kick-drum or delay pedal.  And they love performing fresh renditions of eclectic covers of all genres done with the beautiful sounds of acoustic bluegrass instruments.



Their latest album, "Hideaway" had a single, "Down to the River" debuted by Bluegrass Situation and two singles placed on Spotify's Official Editorial "New Grass" Playlist.  The album that was released just last August already has over 370k Spotify streams.



Recently they have been venturing further and further from Nashville, playing on festivals such as ROMP, Americanafest, Official IBMA Showcase, Albino Skunk and a slew of other small festivals, clubs, events and house concerts. 



Currently they are in residence at The Countrypolitan in Nashville, where they play every week for locals and tourists from across the country who come to Nashville looking for a great, authentic music experience. 



The residency also features regular guest appearances by some of Nashville’s greatest young bluegrass players including Frank Evans (Bronwyn Keith-Hines, Slocan Ramblers), Sasha Ostrovsky (Darius Rucker), Josey Toney(Haily Whitters), Josh Rilko (Sierra Ferrell, Lindsey Lou), Oliver Craven (Stray Birds, Sierra Ferrell), Alex Genova (Fireside Collective, Jason Carter) Tony Aichelle (Travis Tritt, Morgan Wallen), Larry Cook (Tony Trishka), Brenna MacMillan Ben Plotnick on Fiddle, Mandolin, Bass, Dobro, and Banjo. Music 8:30-11:30 pm $10 cover at the door.

title: The Congdon Griffin Band
description:
The Congdon Griffin Band plays the incredible original music of Mountain Express "Best of WNC" winners Eric Congdon, and Hope Griffin. This dynamic 5 piece effortlessly blends Rock, Folk, and Blues, with their unique original sound, while breathing new life into classic covers.



The Congdon Griffin Band blends the raw energy of rock 'n' roll, with the soulful essence of Americana, and twists it in Folk, creating a musical journey that resonates with heart and grit. Led by the electrifying riffs of Eric Congdon and the hauntingly beautiful melodies of Hope Griffin, their sound weaves a tapestry of sonic landscapes. The rhythm section, anchored by Sam Barker's rock solid bass lines, the smooth sounds of Jackson Dulaney's pedal & lap steel and Tyler Matthews' dynamic drumming, propels the band forward with an undeniable groove. Together, they craft a distinct sound that captures the spirit of the open road and the soul of American roots music.
